title: Choose the error-page structure
question: Three recovery layouts in the existing SSC navy-and-crest world. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Errata strip and letter
options.thesis: A live status strip names what happened; a letter below explains it and offers one way home.
options.viewport: Light admin page. A navy strip across the top says Missing page or Something broke. Below, a letter: serif headline, one calm paragraph, navy primary button, ghost Go back.
options.risk: Reads like a memo if the strip is stiff and the letter is long.

raised.raise: The strip is a live now-marker: missing versus crash is always visible.
Go back retraces the exact trail, not a generic Home.
The letter sits as a correction slip, not a dead-end wall.
Missing-page and crash are two distinct states of the same letter.

options.label: Login-kin recovery card
options.thesis: Recovery lives in the same centered white card on navy atmosphere they already trust from signing in.
options.viewport: Full navy field, faint ACSSCO crest. White card: crest, This page isn't here, one sentence, navy Take me home, ghost Go back.
options.risk: Looks like a broken login if the card still feels like a form.

options.label: Quiet desk note
options.thesis: A short note on the ordinary paper-white work surface, as if someone left a helpful slip on the desk.
options.viewport: White work page, no sidebar. Small crest, serif headline, muted one-sentence help, navy button and ghost back.
options.risk: Too modest -- people may not notice they have left their work.

options.label: Step-row recovery
options.thesis: Recovery as a sixteen-step timeline with a chase light for now.
options.viewport: A step row of recovery actions with a chase light on the current one.
options.case: Loses audience identification and clarity: SSC staff do not recover by punching a sequencer.
options.risk: Turns a calm campus error into a toy instrument.
options.kept: Always show where now is -- the status strip.

options.label: Shoebox card flip
options.thesis: Error as one card in a stack; Back retraces the exact trail.
options.viewport: A single recovery card with a visible Back that retraces the trail.
options.case: Holds the back-trail idea; loses identification -- campus staff do not think in HyperCard stacks.
options.risk: Novelty of card-flip motion without helping recovery.
options.kept: Go back retraces the exact trail.

options.label: Errata slip
options.thesis: Error as a vermilion errata slip laid over the work.
options.viewport: A correction slip hinged over the page, not a wall.
options.case: The slip metaphor is friendly; the full acetate system fights the established campus UI.
options.risk: A second material world on a page that already has one.
options.kept: The letter is a correction slip, not a dead-end wall.

options.label: Hall-grid destinations
options.thesis: A stamp-size grid of places they could go next.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnails of Home, Login, Events, Scan.
options.case: A lost person needs one next step, not a hall map.
options.kept: One circled next step, not a menu of forty.

options.label: Ascent route
options.thesis: You are at depth; the page draws the vertical route home.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile with Home as the surface.
options.case: The metaphor fights a campus attendance console.
options.kept: A visible route home, not a maze.

options.label: Failed vs slack
options.thesis: Missing-page and crash as two structural states of one body.
options.viewport: A force diagram that slacks on 404 and fails on crash.
options.case: State distinction is useful; the sculpture is not this audience.
options.risk: An engineering toy on a staff error page.
options.kept: 404 and crash stay visually distinct states.
